questions.question: Ashish covers 72 km at a speed of 45 km/h by bike, 28 km at a speed of 4 km/h by bicycle, and another 160 km at a speed of 20 km/h by car. Find his average speed (in km/h) for the whole journey. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ashish covers 72 km at a speed of 45 km/h by bike, 28 km at a speed of 4 km/h by bicycle, and another 160 km at a speed of 20 km/h by car.

**Formula used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

**Calculation:**

Total Distance = 72 km + 28 km + 160 km

⇒ Total Distance = 260 km

Time by bike = 72 km / 45 km/h

⇒ Time by bike = 1.6 hours

Time by bicycle = 28 km / 4 km/h

⇒ Time by bicycle = 7 hours

Time by car = 160 km / 20 km/h

⇒ Time by car = 8 hours

Total Time = 1.6 hours + 7 hours + 8 hours

⇒ Total Time = 16.6 hours

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 260 km / 16.6 hours

⇒ Average Speed ≈ 15.66 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: A train crosses two persons travelling at 4 km/h and 6 km/h in the same direction in 12 sec and 14 sec, respectively. The speed of the train is ______.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A train crosses two persons in the same direction in 12 sec and 14 sec respectively

Speed of the two persons is 4 km/h and 6 km/h 

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time 

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the train be S and its length be L 

Now, it crosses first person in 12 sec i.e. (12)/(3600) = (1)/(300) h at 4 km/h

Relative speed ,as they move in the same direction = S - 4 

⇒ Distance = Speed × Time 

⇒ L = ( S - 4 ) × (1)/(300) ..............(1)

Also, it crosses second person in 14 sec i.e. (14)/(3600 ) = (7)/(1800) h at 6 km/h 

Relative speed = S - 6

⇒ L = ( S - 6 ) × (7)/(1800) ............(2) 

From equation (1) and (2) we get 

⇒ (S - 4) × (1)/(300) = (S - 6) × (7)/(1800 )

⇒ ( S - 4 ) = ( S - 6 ) × (7)/(6 )

⇒ 6S - 24 = 7S - 42 

⇒ S = 18 km/h 

**Hence, speed of the train is 18 km/h.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** Let the speed of the train = y km/hr

Distance = Speed × Time

A train passes a man or a pole covered its length so the distance covered by the train is the same in both cases.

⇒ (y - 4) × 12 = (y - 6) × 14

⇒ 6y - 24 = 7y - 42

⇒ y = 18

**∴ The speed of the train is 18 km/hr.**

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 20 km/h, while the river is flowing at a speed of 8 km/h and the time taken to cover a certain distance upstream is 6 h more than the time taken to cover the same distance downstream. Find the distance.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of boat in still water (Vb) = 20 km/h

Speed of stream (Vs) = 8 km/h

Extra time upstream = 6 h

**Formula used:**

Speed downstream = Vb + Vs

Speed upstream = Vb - Vs

Time = Distance/Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Speed downstream = 20 + 8 = 28 km/h

Speed upstream = 20 - 8 = 12 km/h

Let distance be D, time downstream Td, and time upstream Tu. Tu = Td + 6

Distance same for both:

Downstream: D = 28 × Td

Upstream: D = 12 × (Td + 6)

⇒ 28 × Td = 12 × (Td + 6)

⇒ 28Td = 12Td + 72 16Td = 72 Td = 4.5

⇒ D = 28 × 4.5 = 126 km

**The distance is 126 km.**

questions.question: Geeta runs 5/2 times as fast as Babita. In a race, if Geeta gives a lead of 40 m to Babita, find the distance from the starting point where both of them will meet (correct up to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of speeds (Geeta : Babita) = 5 : 2

Since time is constant, Distance ratio = Speed ratio = 5 : 2

Difference in distance (Lead) = 5 − 2 = 3 units

3 units → 40 m

Distance from start (Geeta's total distance) = 5 units = (40 ÷ 3) × 5 = 200 ÷ 3 ≈ 66.67 m

**∴ The correct answer is 66.67 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Geeta = 5/2 × Speed of Babita

Lead given to Babita = 40 m

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8e111aa4b516ba1a065e38b23005ef18c6e237fc517c85e3d2df0f10667dac5b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the speed of Babita be 2x and the speed of Geeta be 5x.

⇒ Let the meeting point be at a distance D from the starting point.

⇒ Since they meet at the same time:

⇒ Time taken by Geeta = Time taken by Babita

⇒ D ÷ 5x = (D − 40) ÷ 2x

⇒ D ÷ 5 = (D − 40) ÷ 2

⇒ 2D = 5 × (D − 40)

⇒ 2D = 5D − 200

⇒ 3D = 200

⇒ D = 200 ÷ 3 = 66.666...

⇒ D ≈ 66.67 m

**∴ The correct answer is 66.67 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Races

When two people move in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = V₁ − V₂.

Distance-Speed Relationship

If time is constant, distance is directly proportional to speed (D₁/D₂ = S₁/S₂). If distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).

Concept of Lead

A "lead of x meters" means the slower runner starts x meters ahead of the faster runner. To meet, the faster runner must cover this extra distance using their relative speed.</p

questions.question: A and B run a 12 km race on a circular track of length 1200 m. They complete one round in 300 seconds and 400 seconds, respectively. After how much time from start will the faster person meet the slower person for the last time?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B run a 12 km race 

Length of circular track = 1200 m

Time taken by A to complete the first round = 300 seconds

Time taken by B to complete the first round = 400 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time 

**Calculation:**

Here,

We have 12 km i.e. 12000 m race in a circular track of the length of 1200 m.

Number of round to complete the race = 12000/1200 = 10 rounds

Now,

Time taken by A to complete the first round = 300 seconds

For 10 rounds it will take 300 × 10 = 3000 seconds 

Now,

When A and B both start running,

First meet will take place in L.C.M (300,400) seconds = 1200 sec

Next meet will take place = 1200 × 2 = 2400 seconds

For next meet,

Time would be 3600 seconds, which is Not possible as A completes the race in 3000 seconds

But, to complete 10 rounds A takes 3000 seconds. So, time cannot be more than 3000 seconds

So, faster person will meet the slower person last time at 2400 seconds

**Hence, A will meet B last time at 2400 seconds**.

questions.question: Two trains of lengths 200 m and 250 m are running on parallel rail tracks at speeds of 68 km/h and 50 km/h, respectively. In how much time (in seconds) will they cross each other if they are running in the same direction?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of first train = 200 m

Length of second train = 250 m

Speed of first train = 68 km/h

Speed of second train = 50 km/h

**Concept used:**

To convert speeds from km/h to m/s, we use the formula: speed in m/s = speed in km/h × 5/18

When both trains are running in the same direction, their relative speed = speed of first train - speed of second train.

**Formula used:**

Time taken to cross each other = Total distance / Relative speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Relative speed = 68 - 50 = 18 km/hr

⇒ Speed in m/s = 18 × 5/18 = 5 m/s

Total distance to be covered for the trains to cross each other completely = sum of their lengths = 200 m + 250 m = 450 m

Time taken to cross each other = Total distance / Relative speed

⇒ Time = 450 / 5 = 90 seconds

**Hence, it will take 90 seconds for the two trains to cross each other.**

questions.question: A man covers a certain distance by bike. If he covers 25% of the distance at the speed of 25 km/h, 50% of the distance at the speed of 50 km/h and the remaining distance at the speed of 12.5 km/h, find his average speed over the whole journey.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed1 = 25 km/h for 25%, Speed2 = 50 km/h for 50%, Speed3 = 12.5 km/h for 25%

**Formula Used:**

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

**Calculation:**

Let total distance = D km

Distance covered at Speed1 ⇒ 0.25D, Time1 ⇒ (0.25D) / 25

Distance covered at Speed2 ⇒ 0.5D, Time2 ⇒ (0.5D) / 50

Distance covered at Speed3 ⇒ 0.25D, Time3 ⇒ (0.25D) / 12.5

Total time ⇒ (0.25D/25) + (0.5D/50) + (0.25D/12.5)

⇒ D/100 + D/100 + D/50

⇒ (D/100) + (D/100) + (2D/100)

⇒ 4D/100

⇒ D/25

Average speed ⇒ D / (D/25)

⇒ 25 km/h

**Man's average speed over the whole journey is 25 km/h.**

questions.question: The speeds of two bodies are in the ratio 2 : 3. If the difference in the time taken to cover 50 m is 10 sec, then find the difference in their speeds.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of two bodies speed = 2 : 3

Distance = 50 m

Difference between time taken = 10 sec

**Concept Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the speed of two bodies be 2x and 3x respectively.

⇒ Time taken by first body to cover 50 m = (50)/(2x)

⇒ Time taken by second body to cover 50 m = (50)/(3x)

⇒ According to the question,

⇒ (50)/(2x)-(50)/(3x) = 10

⇒ (150-100)/(6x) = 10

⇒ 50 = 10 × 6x

⇒ x = (50)/(60)=(5)/(6)

⇒ Difference in speed = 3x – 2x = x = (5)/(6) m/sec.

**Therefore, the difference between the speed of two bodies is (5)/(6) m/sec.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

We know, when distance is constant, then speed ∝ 1/time

The speeds of two bodies are in the ratio 2 : 3, then, time ratio of two bodies 3 : 2

Difference in the time (3 - 2) = 1 unit → 10 sec, then 3 unit → 10 × 3 = 30 sec and 2 unit → 10 × 2 = 20 sec

So, body 1 takes time to cover 50 m is 30 sec, Speed = 50/30 = 5/3m/s

And body 2 takes time to cover 50 m is 20 sec, Speed = 50/20 = 5/2 m/s

Speed difference = (5/2 - 5/3) = 5/6 m/s

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 250 m. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. Assuming that the speed of the thief is 10 km/h and that of the policeman is 12 km/h, how far would the thief have run before he is caught?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between the thief and the policeman = 250 m

Speed of the thief = 10 km/h or (25)/(9) m/s

Speed of the policeman = 12 km/h or (10)/(3) m/s

**Formula used:**

Speed = (Distance)/(Time)

**Concept used:**

Relative speed = Speed of policeman - Speed of thief

**Calculation:**

The relative speed of the thief and the policeman = 12 - 10 = 2 km/h or 2((5)/(18)) = ((5)/(9)) m/s

Time taken by the policeman to catch the thief

⇒ T = (250)/((frac{5){9})}

⇒ T = 50 × 9 = 450 s

Now Distance traveled by the thief before getting caught

⇒ D = (25)/(9) × 450

⇒ D = 25 × 50 = 1250 m or 1.25 km

**∴ The thief ran 1.25 km before he is caught.**
